# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. ===AGENTS=== # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. content.text:
So clean approach: static index.html (HTML type) served by default-start. No npm needed. We can build a high-quality canvas game with no build step. Use HTML/CSS/JS modules. Need make it beautiful, playable, responsive/touch controls per Agents.md, and verify by browser screenshot via playwright.

We should design a game with day farming and night tower defense. Let's think deeply about game design and implementation.

Game concept:
- "Hollowmere" / "Moonacre Farm" - cozy pixel-art-ish farm by day, defend from shadow creatures by night.
- Day cycle: day phase ~90 seconds. Player moves around a grid farm with WASD/arrow keys and touch joystick. Till soil, plant seeds, water, harvest. Sell crops at market? Use coins to buy seeds and build towers. Day ends automatically or when player sleeps at bed (press E near bed) — but let's make day length maybe 120 seconds and can rest at bed to start night early. Day progress changes lighting (morning→golden→dusk).
- Night phase: tower defense. Fixed path from dark forest gate to farmhouse. Player places towers during day? Or at night? The loop: prepare defenses by day, survive waves at night. Should be accessible. Night begins, waves of shadow imps march along a winding path toward the farmhouse. Towers placed strategically along path shoot. Player can also attack with a lantern/slingshot? Maybe player has a "lantern blast" ability on click. But core: towers.
- Between nights, earn essence/crops, buy towers, plant crops that generate gold, upgrades. Win condition survive 5 nights? Endless scoring maybe. Need win/lose state and restart.

Could be more Stardew: crops grow over days, each day you water. Harvest crops for gold. Shop at farm stand to buy seeds/towers. Build towers with gold. Night waves reward "moon shards" spent on tower upgrades? Simpler one currency "coins" to buy seeds and towers. Crops produce coins; night rewards coins. If enemy reaches farmhouse, lose hearts (lantern health 10). Survive 7 nights to win? Let's design a 7-night campaign with escalating waves and a boss on night 7? This may be scope-heavy but doable.

Rendering: Canvas 2D with a rich hand-drawn / pixel aesthetic. Use procedural drawing: grass tiles with texture variation, tilled soil, water pond, trees with shadows, house with windows glowing at night, path, fences, fireflies at night, stars/moon, light radii, particle effects, floating text. Smooth day/night lighting overlay, warm sunset colors. Sound: WebAudio procedural ambience, chimes, attack sounds, maybe toggleable music. Need mobile support.

Architecture:
- index.html with canvas and HUD overlays, title screen, panels.
- styles.css for polished UI with custom fonts (import Google Fonts? network maybe unavailable; use system fonts or embed. Better use CSS font stack with serif display "Georgia"? But we can load Google font - preview might have internet. Avoid dependency: use @import? Use local fallback. Could include "Cormorant Garamond" via Google Fonts; but offline render risk. Use system fonts: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", "Georgia" for display, and monospace for numbers. Could also draw text with canvas.
- js/main.js or game modules:
  - state, loop, input, audio, world, player, farming, towers, enemies, waves, particles, UI.

Maybe split into ES modules: src/main.js, src/engine.js, src/world.js, src/game.js, src/render.js, src/audio.js, src/ui.js. But static relative module imports work. Need ensure server MIME .js application/javascript (yes).

Testing: game state automation. Add a debug hook `window.__moonacre` with methods for screenshots and maybe URL params to skip to phases. We should test with Playwright ourselves.

We have plenty of time. Let's aim for quality.

Important: "Stardew farming by day, tower defense at night" literal. We should have both modes visibly. Strong title screen. Maybe game called "Moonglow Hollow" or "Nightbloom Farm". Let's choose "Moonglow Hollow" - cozy farm under a curse. Day phase and night phase.

Core loop:
- 7 days/nights. Each day lasts 75 seconds game time (1 real second = maybe 1 game minute). Start day 1 dawn. Can plant/harvest/build anytime during day; night starts automatically at dusk or via sleeping in bed. Maybe pressing "N" to ring the bell to call the night early (with confirmation if in combat?).
- Tower placement allowed day and night? Tower defense games allow placement during waves; to keep flow, allow building anytime but placement only on buildable pads along path. Each pad is a circle of stones with cost 35 coins. Clicking a pad opens radial build menu with 3 tower types: Lantern (single-target), Sprinkler (slow), Scarecrow (AoE splash)? Use thematic towers:
  - Lantern Post (cost 40): fires bolts at nearest enemy medium range.
  - Thorn Vine (cost 55): slows and damages enemies in area, maybe line.
  - Beehive (cost 65): rapid short-range with swarm bolts.
  - Moonwell (cost 90) maybe splash.
Let's keep 3 tower types to keep UI clean:
  - Sun Lantern: 45g, balanced, range 130, damage 12, fire rate 0.8s.
  - Frost Sprinkler: 60g, slows 35%, range 110, damage 3.
  - Bramble Totem: 80g, lobbed AoE, range 150, damage 24/splash, slow rate.
  Upgrades? Could add 2 upgrade levels each with cost.

- Farm plots grid: 6x4 or 5x4 area. Tilling via click on plot or near player press Space. Plant selected seed on tilled plot; water; crops grow each day transition (need water). Harvest by click or Space near. Maybe direct click interactions simpler and mobile friendly. Player walks around; click tile to till/plant/water/harvest if within range. But for mobile use touch to tap? We can make tap-to-act within range regardless. Good.

Crops: turnip (seeds 10, sells 25, 1 day), sunberry (25 → 70, 2 days), moonflower (50 → 160, 3 days). Water requirement: if planted but not watered that day, growth pauses. Visual growth stages. Player has watering can with limited water 8, refill at pond/well. That adds depth. But could be tedious. We can auto-water? Let's implement watering can capacity 12 and refill at pond by walking near/clicking. Each plot needs water once per day; growth at day rollover. On day 1 you plant and water, next morning growth stage advances. Harvest sells automatically? Better inventory: harvested crops stored, sell at stand with click, or auto-add coins with floating "+25g". For casual game auto-sell on harvest is simplest and satisfying. But shop needs seeds. Let's auto-sell.

- Night waves: 7 nights. Each night has 3 waves? Could be continuous spawn over ~60s with increasing intensity. Enemies follow a path through the farm (fixed waypoints) and if reach farmhouse damage. Towers auto-target. Player during night: move around, use lantern ability (click/tap or Space) with cooldown, plus can repair? We can allow player to throw a lantern flare at cursor causing small AoE damage with cooldown. Also towers can be built during night if enough coins. Player health? Farmhouse has 10 "hearth" hearts; each enemy that reaches it deals 1-2 damage and disappears. If hearts hit 0, game over. Surviving night gives coins and resets hearts partially? Each night clear reward and dawn. Maybe farmhouse health restores 2 each dawn.

- Waves: Night 1: 8 shadowlings. Night 2: 14 + 2 brutes. Night 3... up to night 7 boss "Hollow King" with more HP. Win after night 7.

- Day/night cycle: Day 1 dawn → day length 60s → dusk (5s) → night 1 (~70s) → dawn day 2. Could be 60s day and 60s night. Add pause menu. Maybe 75s each; game 7 cycles ~17 min. Fine.

- Score: coins, nights survived; end screen with stats.

- Objective/quest panel: "Day 1 — Till, plant, water" "Night 1 — Survive the shadows". Toast hints.

Visual:
- Isometric-ish top-down? Simpler 2D top-down with slight 3/4 perspective (sprites drawn as upright objects). Background 1280x760 world with grass, dirt paths, pond, farmhouse at right, field left-center, forest border top-left where enemies spawn. Towers pads near path. Path starts from dark forest gate top-left, winds down and right to farmhouse door.
- Use layered canvas: ground, crops, entities sorted by y, lighting overlay, particles, UI DOM.
- Instead of tile rendering super complex, procedurally paint textures to offscreen canvas at load: grass base with noise, path, soil plots. Draw static scene once to background canvas; dynamic objects drawn each frame.
- Style: painterly pixel/vector mix. Need crisp and polished. Use palette: earthy greens, warm cream, deep indigo night, amber lantern glow.
- Add lighting: during night, overlay dark blue with alpha ~0.72, then use "destination-out"/radial gradients for lanterns, house windows, moonwells, player lantern. Canvas compositing: draw overlay onto separate light canvas: fill dark, add radial gradients with 'destination-out' to cut holes, draw "light" colors with screen blend on main. Simpler: draw shadow overlay on main canvas with globalCompositeOperation 'multiply'? To cut holes, use an offscreen light canvas: black/dark fill, then use 'destination-out' radial gradients at light sources, then draw with 'source-over' onto main. That creates darkness with holes (not additive warm light). Add warm additive radial gradients on main with 'screen'. Good.

- Ambient particles: pollen/fireflies, leaves, rain? Night fireflies.
- Trees gently sway; crops bounce; water shimmer; chimney smoke; stars.

- UI: top bar with Day/Night indicator, phase timer arc, coins, seeds selected, watering can, hearts, wave info; bottom hotbar (seeds, tools) and buttons (Build, Codex?, Sound, Pause). Left-side objective card. Floating interaction prompts near player (E). Title screen full overlay with animated background, illustrated logo. Shop modal, tower build modal, night results, game over, victory, help.

Controls:
- WASD/arrow keys move. Shift run? Space context action (till/plant/water/harvest/interact), 1-3 select seed, Q/E cycle? For touch: virtual joystick left and action buttons right, plus tapping world. We'll implement both.
- Mouse click on field/plots/towers? We can support pointer movement to aim lantern at night and click to use ability. On mobile, the right action button "Lantern" blasts at nearest enemy or facing direction.

- Save? Not needed; but can use localStorage for best night. Could add. Avoid complexity.

Implementation detail plan:

Files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js (bootstrap, game loop)
- src/config.js maybe
- src/audio.js
- src/input.js
- src/world.js (map, plots, pads, path, background rendering)
- src/game.js (state, day/night, farming, towers, enemies)
- src/render.js (draw world/entities/effects)
- src/ui.js (DOM updates, modals)

Could be 3000+ lines. Need ensure no bugs. We can write carefully.

Maybe simpler: fewer modules but organized. Let's design in detail.

World layout (logical 1280x720, scaled to fit):
- World size W=1280 H=720. Camera maybe fixed with slight shake, no scrolling, scaled responsively. 16:9 landscape. On mobile portrait, letterbox? Better responsive canvas: keep world aspect 16:9 but fill with cover? Touch controls overlay. Could use CSS scale with object-fit; world camera adjusts. For portrait, game still visible but letterboxed; controls overlay. We can render at 1280x720 and scale to fit width; in portrait, height may be small. Maybe dynamic world viewport with camera following player and zoom? That's more complex but better mobile. But a fixed farm map can fit. On mobile 390x844, a 16:9 game in middle leaves lots of empty; acceptable if HUD on top/bottom. Could use world in 4:3-ish? Hmm.

Alternative: responsive canvas with camera that fits width, and background scaled to fit. For desktop 1440x900, canvas 16:9 at width 1440 height 810. For mobile, canvas 390x844; draw world with zoom out (scale 0.55) showing width 1280? That would make objects tiny. Better portrait mode with camera following player and zoom (view ~640x1000) and world 1280x720 doesn't fit height. We can design world 1600x1000 and camera follow on mobile; desktop shows whole map? Complex.

Maybe make the game world fixed 1280x720 and canvas fills available viewport with "meet" letterboxing. On mobile, it appears as a landscape strip in middle, playable with touch overlay. Agents.md says support mobile usable controls; technically yes. But polished mobile wants better. We can set game container aspect-ratio 16/9 max height and allow rotate hint on portrait ("Rotate for the best view") while still playable. Many games do that.

Could use CSS scale for portrait: canvas container fills 100vw/100vh; draw scene with camera zoomed based on aspect. Implement view transform: world base 1280x720. Compute scale = max(vw/1280, vh/720)? That's cover, cropping. For portrait crop sides heavily. Camera can follow player and show 640x720 (portrait) with scale = vh/720, x camera clamped. That yields a nice mobile experience: world 1280 wide, viewport shows ~640 wide, following player. Desktop shows full world. This is doable! Rendering transform: scale = min? Let's define viewport CSS px. Choose desired visible world height = 720 for landscape; for portrait, we can show a 720-high slice, width = vh? Actually if we set scale = cssHeight/720 for all, portrait 844 => 1.17, visible world width = 390/1.17=333, too narrow. That's very zoomed in. Hmm.

Better scale = max(cssWidth/1280, cssHeight/720)?? For portrait, cssWidth/1280=0.3, cssHeight/720=1.17 -> 1.17 too zoomed. Use fit: min = 0.3, view height = 844/0.3 = 2813 > world height. Not good.

We could design world 1280x960 (4:3) and camera. Desktop view shows whole width at scale width/1280; mobile camera follows. If world and viewport varies, camera follow with zoom fixed at 1 world unit = ~? Let's think: Let scale = clamp(cssWidth / 900, 0.55, 1.3) for mobile? Visible world width = cssWidth/scale. For 390 width, scale 0.55 => 709 wide, height 1534 -> world 960 not enough. Camera view height > world. Could allow background beyond.

Maybe simpler: fixed world 1280x720, render with scale = cssWidth/1280 for landscape; if portrait, scale = cssWidth/700 and vertical camera follow, so visible world width 700? 390/700=0.557, visible height 844/0.557=1515 > 720 impossible. Need add vertical world padding.

I think fixed 16:9 letterbox with rotate hint is acceptable. We can make it polished: On portrait, show game in landscape orientation using CSS transform rotate? Some games force orientation. Better to just render with object-fit contain, leaving a beautiful dusk background around it, controls overlay below within screen. But game area small.

Actually touch direct interactions make fixed view fine if canvas is wide. We can add an orientation overlay on portrait that suggests rotating, with "Play anyway". Hmm.

Let's consider desktop-first (verification screenshot desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844). The capture will screenshot title/start. Auto-start clicks start selector maybe. We should make title and game look great at 1440x900. Mobile screenshot just needs not broken.

Maybe use landscape canvas that fills width, header top, bottom HUD. On mobile it's 390x219 game area plus HUD, still okay. But tap targets need larger overlays. Hmm.

We can make the canvas container flex-grow, with world aspect 16:9, letterbox inside. The rest of screen used by HUD. That's fine.

Let's now plan the game specifics in code.

Game state:
```

const state = {
 mode:'title'|'playing'|'paused'|'shop'|'build'|'help'|'gameover'|'victory',
 phase:'day'|'night'|'dawn'|'dusk',
 day:1,
 phaseTime:0, phaseDuration: 90 (day), 75 (night),
 coins: 120,
 hearts: 10, maxHearts:10,
 water: 10, maxWater:10,
 selectedSeed:0,
 seeds: [turnip: 0 ...]? Actually seeds inventory? 
}
```
Should seeds be inventory or buy directly? Let's have seed inventory counts purchased from shop. Starting: 3 turnip seeds, 0 others. Shop sells seed packets (3 for 30g?). Hmm. For simplicity: selected seed type, each planting costs coins equal seed cost, no inventory. Shop is for buying towers? Could skip seed shop; planting costs coins directly. That's intuitive: "Turnip seed — 10g; harvest 28g". Day 1 starts 70 coins, plant 3 turnips. This avoids shop for seeds. But then shop only for towers? Tower build happens on pads. Maybe no shop modal at all. But a seed menu/hotbar is useful.

We can have hotbar:
1. Hoe (free, till)
2. Watering can
3. Turnip seeds (10g)
4. Sunberry seeds (24g)
5. Moonflower seeds (45g)

Context action with selected tool on nearest plot. Clicking/tapping a plot also acts. When plot is tilled and seed selected, planting charges coins. Watering can consumes water. Harvest automatic with any tool? Press Space on mature crop harvests regardless.

Refill water at pond/well.

Crops:
```
turnip: cost 10, sell 28, growDays 1, color cream/purple
sunberry: cost 24, sell 72, growDays 2
moonflower: cost 45, sell 170, growDays 3
```
Growth requires watered each day. At day rollover, if plot.watered then growth++; reset watered false. If mature, can harvest anytime. A mature crop doesn't need water. Plant watering same day: newly planted plot starts watered? If you plant, set watered=false; you must water. That’s fine. Maybe seed starts with water false. Hints tell.

Plots: 4 rows x 6 cols in field. Coordinates: x 170..490, y 250..500. Tile 52. Could draw 24 plots. Let's use 5 cols x 4 rows = 20. Each plot center coordinate.

World map design:
- Farmhouse: right side x 960-1200, y 190-400. Door at (1080, 400). Path from forest (x 60,y 170) winds: waypoints [(30,120),(220,150),(360,260),(520,300),(640,380),(800,380),(900,430),(1010,450),(1080,430),(1080,400)]. Hmm field is left-center. Pads near path.
- Forest top-left/top edge with dark trees where enemies spawn.
- Pond bottom-left (x 90-330, y 560-690) with dock; well maybe in field.
- Field center-left x 250-640 y 260-500.
- Farmhouse right x 930-1210 y 160-410. Porch. Warm windows.
- Trees along boundaries, bushes, flowers, fences, stone path. 
- Tower pads at e.g. (360,180), (520,240), (700,260), (780,460), (930,520), (620,500), (470,390), (860,330). 8 pads. Buildable placement only at pads. Need path not overlapping.

Maybe a more serpentine path from forest left edge to house:
Path waypoints:
A (0, 130) forest gate (top-left)

This weaves through map. Field could be at x 180-560 y 300-520, below path. Pads near bends.

Need draw path as thick bezier/polyline with textured edges; use smoothed path. Enemy movement via Catmull-Rom or linear interpolation with waypoints. We can use linear segments with round joins, fine.

Field must not overlap path. Let's place field 5 cols x 4 rows starting x=160,y=320, tile 54 → width 270, height 216 ends at 430,536. Path B..E around y 160-300, so okay. Pond bottom-right? Let's redesign simpler:

World 1280x720:
- House at top-right (x 950-1220, y 100-330), door at (1085, 330). Path leads to door.
- Path from forest gate left-center-top (0,180) → (170,190) → (330,250) → (500,250) → (640,330) → (760,430) → (900,450) → (1010,380) → (1085,340).
- Field left-bottom: x 130-520, y 380-600 (5x4 tiles 56? 5*56=280; 4*56=224 ends 604). But path at y 250 above, fine.
- Pond bottom-right x 900-1180 y 540-690.
- Pads: (300,150) near path top; (610,180); (740,300); (1000,520); (760,550); (500,650); (880,280); (420,520)? Need 6-8.
- Farmhouse yard with fence, well at (600,420)? Maybe well near field for refill.
- Trees border entire map and forest left top.

Player spawn (700,500). Camera fixed.

Enemy path approach: spawn at (-30,180) moving right; target house door (1085,340). Enemies at end "attack" house and disappear with heart loss.

Towers:
- Pad positions at least 90 px from path so range matters. Tower range 130-170.
- Build UI: click pad opens small popover DOM positioned over canvas? Easier draw build menu on canvas with clickable options. But DOM UI is more polished. We can have a tower build panel modal (bottom) listing towers with costs when pad selected. Click tower card then build. Or clicking pad cycles? Let's implement: click pad → selection ring and a "Build here" radial menu on canvas with 3 circular buttons labeled by icons/cost, click one → build if coins. This is nice and game-like, and supports touch. We can draw with canvas and handle pointer hit tests. Maybe also show panel with descriptions. Simpler interactive: clicking pad opens a DOM "build tray" bottom center with 3 cards and a close button, selected pad highlighted. That's accessible and easier. Build tray also available via keyboard B selecting nearest pad? We'll handle pad click/tap. During night maybe allow building too (good).

- Tower upgrade: click built tower → tray showing "Upgrade — cost" and "Sell +50%". Towers level 1-2 maybe 3. Add range/damage scaling. Nice.

- Tower visuals:
  - Sun Lantern: wooden post with glowing golden lantern, rotating? shoots beam projectile.
  - Frost Sprinkler: copper sprinkler spinning, blue pulses aura slows.
  - Bramble Totem: gnarled wood totem with glowing green eyes, lobs seed bomb with AoE.

Enemies:

  - Moth? maybe flying straight ignoring path? No, keep path.
  - Boss "Hollow Stag" after night 7: speed 18, hp 1200, damage 5, aura.
  - Maybe "Thornling" heals? Keep 3 types.
- Health bars above enemies when damaged. Death particles (dark petals).
- Wave composition by night:
  - night 1: 8 shade
  - night 2: 10 shade + 3 wisp
  - night 3: 12 shade + 4 wisp + 1 brute
  - etc. Total waves. Spawn groups.
We can implement a spawn queue: list of {type, delay}. Night lasts until queue empty and enemies dead. Then result screen at dawn (or automatically transition). Survive reward: 40 + 15*night coins; hearts +2. Then dawn.
- Night timer maybe counts down to dawn but if enemies remain at 0, they persist? Simpler dynamic wave. Add "Night 1/7". At end show a brief results toast then transition to day with sunrise animation.

Player:

- Interaction radius 80 around plot/pad/well/bed. Selected contextual target highlight. Space action: if near mature crop harvest; else apply selected tool to nearest plot; if near well refill; if near bed sleep (start night early); if near pad open build. Mouse click on plot: if player too far, set walk target and auto-interact on arrival? Nice UX. Implement click-to-move with click marker; player walks toward target and then acts. But direct interaction if within range. Clicking plot far away sets `moveTarget` and `pendingAction`. During night, clicking on tower pad maybe build. Aim lantern via cursor.

Maybe complexity; but clicking farm plots from afar and walking there automatically feels good. We'll implement:
- pointerdown on canvas: if UI open ignore. Determine world position. If mode night and click not on pad/tower, fire lantern toward point (if cooldown and within? any distance). During day: if click plot or pad or well, set move target adjacent and pendingAction; if already near execute. Also allow click anywhere => move target (desktop). On touch, tapping world also moves (maybe).
- keyboard Space triggers nearest context.

The player's lantern blast at night: cost? cooldown 4s, deals 35 damage in radius 55 at clicked point, range maybe 260. Visual flare. This gives active agency. On mobile button "FLARE".

Also player can collect "moon motes" dropped by enemies? Night reward coins auto. Maybe enemies drop coins during night? That adds busy work. Instead at night end reward.

Audio:
- WebAudio procedural: day ambient arpeggio pad (soft sine/triangle), night drone + pulse; effects for till, water, plant, harvest, build, shoot, enemy death, hurt, wave start, dawn, victory. Master gain, mute toggle. Start on user gesture. Keep music subtle. Use scheduler maybe. Implement simple ambient chord loop with setInterval? Better use WebAudio oscillators and a sequencer in the game loop. Create audio manager:
  - ensure context on first interaction.
  - playTone(freq, duration, type, volume, slideTo)
  - noise burst for till/water.

UI design:

- HUD:
  Top left: day badge "DAY 1" with small sun/moon icon and phase name; countdown ring.
  Top center: objective card maybe "First Harvest — Till 3 plots, plant turnip seeds, water them."; actually maybe a toast at bottom.
  Top right: coins pill, hearts row, sound/pause buttons.
  Bottom left: hotbar cards with icons drawn by CSS/SVG? We can use emoji? Emoji rendering inconsistent but easy and colorful. Better draw icons as inline SVG or CSS shapes. Could use emoji for seeds/tools: 🌱💧⛏️? Emoji at 24px looks okay, but style could be inconsistent. We can craft cute SVG icons? That's lots. Use emoji for inventory icons (🪓? hoe).   lctx.fillStyle='rgba(8,10,35,0.78)'; fillRect;
  lctx.globalCompositeOperation='destination-out';
  for each light: radial gradient center alpha 1->0, radius
  lctx.globalCompositeOperation='source-over';
  // draw offscreen onto main

  // then draw warm glows additive
  ctx.globalCompositeOperation='lighter';
  radial gradients color w/ alpha; fill
}

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
